Each source has a corresponding SHA-256 checksum, which is not set to 'SKIP', indicating that the integrity of the downloaded binaries will be verified during the build process.

There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected network locations, or suspicious commands in this file. The use of GitHub Releases for distributing precompiled binaries is common for Rust-based CLI tools like this one, and the presence of verifiable checksums enhances supply-chain security. No scripts or executable logic are present in .SRCINFO — it is purely declarative metadata used by Arch Linux packaging tools. All listed attributes follow standard AUR packaging practices.

The license is properly declared as MIT OR Apache-2.0, matching typical open-source dual-licensing models. The package options exclude debug information (`!debug`), which is acceptable for a binary-only distribution. No post-install hooks, system modifications, or network operations are defined in this file. As .SRCINFO does not contain executable code and only reflects the PKGBUILD's metadata, and since all sources are pinned to specific release versions with valid hashes, there is no evidence of malicious behavior.
